extracted.intended_audience: authors and illustrators of beginning-reader books, children's librarians, and publishers
extracted.subtask_description: Eligibility and evaluation standards for the Theodor Seuss Geisel Award, which recognizes the most distinguished book for beginning readers (text aimed at pre-K through Grade 2) published in English in the United States during the preceding year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage and support the beginning reader
rubrics_metrics.description: The book must encourage and support the beginning reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication in English in the United States during preceding year
rubrics_metrics.description: The book must be published in English in the United States during the preceding year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and function as a beginning-reader book
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no limitations as to the character of the book considered except that it will be original and function successfully as a book for beginning readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes both originality and practical suitability for beginning-reader use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author(s)/illustrator(s) U.S. citizenship or residency
rubrics_metrics.description: The author(s) or illustrator(s) must be citizens or residents of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'author(s) and illustrator(s)' may include co-authors and co-illustrators; awards may be given posthumously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text directed to pre-K through Grade 2
rubrics_metrics.description: The text must be directed at readers from pre-K through Grade 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the target age/grade range for appropriate vocabulary, sentence structure, and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations function as keys or clues to the text
rubrics_metrics.description: The illustrations must function as keys or clues to the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations should support decoding and comprehension rather than merely decorate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction, non-fiction, and poetry eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiction, non-fiction, and poetry are all eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All literary forms are considered as long as they meet beginning-reader suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprints and compilations ineligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Reprints and compilations are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only new, original eligible publications from the preceding year qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter must motivate the child to read
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter must be intriguing enough to motivate the child to read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content should engage and sustain interest for emerging readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: May include short chapters
rubrics_metrics.description: The book may or may not include short 'chapters.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of short chapters is permitted but not required; format should suit beginning-reader needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce new words slowly
rubrics_metrics.description: New words should be added slowly enough to make learning them a positive experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pacing of vocabulary introduction should support confidence and learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetition of words for retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Words should be repeated to ensure knowledge retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategic repetition aids emergent readers in retaining vocabulary and building skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple and straightforward sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentences must be simple and straightforward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sentence complexity should be appropriate to beginning-reader decoding and comprehension abilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum page count
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be a minimum of 24 pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum page count
rubrics_metrics.description: Books may not be longer than 96 pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations demonstrate the story
rubrics_metrics.description: The illustrations must demonstrate the story being told.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations should actively depict narrative action and support readers' understanding of plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successful start-to-finish reading experience
rubrics_metrics.description: The book creates a successful reading experience, from start to finish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall pacing, cohesion, and readability should enable a satisfying emergent-reader experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page-to-page plot advance and page-turning dynamic
rubrics_metrics.description: The plot advances from one page to the next and creates a 'page-turning' dynamic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative momentum and visual/textual cues should encourage continued reading and engagement.
